source.title: tryToParseTime accepts out-of-range hours, minutes and seconds

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
## Summary

`tryToParseTime` (`packages/workflow/src/type-validation.ts`) only checks the shape of a time string with a regex (two-digit hour:minute, optional seconds and UTC offset) and never validates the numeric ranges. As a result impossible values such as `24:00`, `99:00`, `12:60`, `12:30:99` and `99:99` are accepted and returned unchanged.

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
tryToParseTime('99:99');    // returns '99:99', should throw "Value is not a valid time"
tryToParseTime('24:00');    // returns '24:00'
tryToParseTime('12:30:99'); // returns '12:30:99'
```

For comparison, `tryToParseTime('00:00')` returns `'00:00'` and `tryToParseTime('1:30')` is rejected because of the shape.

## Expected behavior

Beyond the shape check, validate the ranges: hour 0-23, minute 0-59, second 0-59. Out-of-range values should throw the same `UserError: Value is not a valid time` as malformed input. Valid boundary values (`00:00`, `23:59:59`) and values with a UTC offset (`12:30+05:30`) should be returned unchanged; the existing shape validation should not change.

## Impact

`validateFieldType` calls this function for the `time` field type, so invalid times currently pass validation into execution data and only fail later in a downstream API, database or scheduling logic (or get stored as bad data), which is costly to debug. The fix is confined to `tryToParseTime` and does not touch other field types.
